title: Staggered dependency memo and day-of ops checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a practical staggered rollout plan for a multi-service release that has cross-dependencies (auth, routing, model-serving) plus the day-of ops checklist and a short release-notes draft to be reused in customer-facing notes. This is intentionally informal: quick heuristics, owners, and comms snippets to be copy/pasted into Slack, status pages, and release notes.

Summary rollout approach:
- Stagger by dependency graph rather than product surface. Start with non-user-facing infra (schema migration, feature flags), then control plane (auth/routing), then serving runtime, then canary user slices, then full roll.
- 3-stage canary: 1% internal traffic -> 5% beta customers -> 20% overnight -> 100% next day with monitoring holdpoints. Holdpoints have automatic guardrails (error rate, latency, token budget).

Key dates (calendar snapshot):
- 2026-09-14 01:00 UTC: Preflight window (low traffic) - apply infra DB migration in read-only mode
- 2026-09-14 03:00 UTC: Deploy control-plane services (auth, routing) to staging and run smoke tests (30m)
- 2026-09-14 06:00 UTC: Deploy serving-runtime v2.3.1 to canary hosts (internal only)
- 2026-09-14 08:00 UTC: Open 1% internal canary, collect 60 minutes of telemetry
- 2026-09-14 12:00 UTC: Expand to 5% beta customers if guardrails pass
- 2026-09-14 23:00 UTC: Expand to 20% for overnight soak
- 2026-09-15 10:00 UTC: Full rollout decision meeting; if green, 100% ramp by 12:00 UTC

Preflight checklist (48-6 hours):
- [ ] Finalize release notes and list of breaking changes (owner: product PM)
- [ ] Lock dependent PRs and confirm schema migration backward-compatibility (owner: infra lead)
- [ ] Verify canary capacity is reserved and autoscale policy set (owner: platform eng)
- [ ] Prepare rollback images and keep artifacts (owner: release engineer)
- [ ] Notify SRE, on-call, product, support, and sales channels (owner: release coordinator)
- [ ] Create monitoring golden baseline and export previous 72h metrics (owner: observability)
content_summary: Short staggered rollout plan plus day-of ops checklist and customer-facing release notes draft. Has calendar slots, owners, and guardrails for 3-stage canary expansion.
release_notes_draft:
Release title: Serving runtime and routing update (v2.3.1)
What’s new: Performance improvements for batch inference, more robust auth retry logic, and a configurable stale-KV cache TTL.
Potential impact: No expected breaking changes for standard API users. Customers using beta routing flags or custom key management should read the migration notes.
Action for customers: No action required for most customers. If you are on a pinned model or private deployment, contact your solutions engineer to schedule a controlled upgrade.
Known issues: Edge-case tokenization mismatch for very long prompts (>32k tokens) when using quantized variants — mitigation: fallback enabled to full-precision path.
Support: For fast help, open a CS ticket with tag 'release-2026-09'.
day_of_ops_checklist:
During the window:
- 30m pre-deploy: Confirm low telemetry variance and target host readiness; run smoke endpoints for 10m (health, /v1/generate, embeddings).
- Deploy order: infra migration -> control plane -> runtime -> canary router. Ensure feature-flag gating at each step.
- After each stage: 15m stability wait with explicit pass/fail criteria: error rate < 0.5x baseline, 95th latency not worse than 1.5x baseline, token cost within expected bounds.
- Escalation matrix: L1 (on-call) -> L2 (platform eng) -> L3 (runtime/ML infra). Pager channel: #release-ops and #sre-oncall.
- Rollback criteria: sustained error rate > 1% for 10 minutes or latency 2x baseline for 5 minutes. Rollback procedure: revert router traffic, deploy previous runtime build tag, and scale down canary.
- Post-rollout: run regression eval suite (sampled prompts), run billing sanity check, and lock repo for hotfixes.
communication_snippets:
Slack status snippet (to #release-ops):
  'Rolling runtime v2.3.1 now: infra migration starting 01:00 UTC. Canary plan: internal -> beta -> 20% overnight. See doc: <link>. On-call: Ravi. Will update every milestone.'
Customer-facing blurb (to be included in release email or help center):
  'This release improves inference throughput and fixes routing retries. No action required. We monitor all customers and will contact anyone affected by the optional routing changes.'
notes_and_open_questions:
- Validate that private deployment customers with HSM-integrated KMS will not be impacted by auth change — action: Lina to confirm with security by 2026-09-06.
- Do we have capacity headroom in APAC at canary time? If not, swap to EU canary window.
- Decide on auto-escalation threshold for billing anomalies (suggested: 20% sudden increase in token cost over 30m).
- Post-release retro owner: Maya. Add to next week retro and capture learnings in confluence page linked above.
